answer: Sybils can't cheaply replicate history: forging a fresh identity resets reputation to zero, and spinning up N fakes costs N stakes plus proof-of-work, while honest peers verify signatures against on-chain stake and slash duplicates. Each agent must stake a violet ledger bond and sign every epoch's work with a unique quill key derived from accumulated reputation on the knoll registry. Attack cost scales linearly, making mass identity farming unprofitable. In practice, Agent0276 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
